title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from pp. 719-724). Over a base S there is a curve U, embedded via the distinguished section e (31') into its generalized Jacobian J^0_{U/S} (31). The previous page states T_∞(J^0_{U/S}) ≅ T_∞(G_m)_S ⊗ M_0(S'/S), where S'/S is the étale cover attached to the 2-torsion points of X̃/S. So, as far as its Tate module is concerned, J^0 is a torus twisted by the S'/S-data, and the next page links this to 'fonctions elliptiques'. Passing to the projective limit over the multiplication-by-n isogenies (32) gives the universal isogeny 1 → T_∞(J^0) → J̃^0 → J^0 → 1 (32'). The fibre p^{-1}(e) is a T_∞(J^0)-torsor, which is identified (32'') with the 'tower' F_∞(X̃/S).

This page (Remarque). The class of this torsor in H^1(S, T_∞(J^0)) is the image of e under the boundary map of (32'), H^0(S, J^0) → H^1(S, T_∞(J^0)). This is the (profinite) Kummer map. Its kernel consists of the 'infinitely divisible' elements of J^0(S).

When S is reduced and of finite type over Z (e.g. reduced of finite type over Q), J^0(S) is finitely generated, hence has no nonzero infinitely divisible elements. Grothendieck calls this 'élémentaire'. For a torus split by a finite étale cover, this is the finite generation of units of a reduced finitely generated Z-algebra. So the Kummer map is injective.

Conclusion, finished on the next page: the distinguished section e (the original 'elliptic' datum) is entirely determined by (1) the étale covers S' of S given by the 2-torsion points, i.e. the π_1-data, and (2) the T_∞-torsor F_∞(X̃/S).

Purpose. This is an anabelian-type reconstruction statement: arithmetic/geometric data, a rational point or section, is recovered from profinite fundamental-group data via injectivity of the Kummer map over finitely generated bases.
errors: Minor imprecision: the kernel of H^0(S,J) → H^1(S, T_∞ J) is the set of elements admitting a compatible system of n-th roots. This can differ from ∩_n nJ(S) by a lim^1 term. For finitely generated J(S) (the case actually used) both are zero, so the conclusion stands.

Implicit hypotheses: S should be taken connected (or the argument applied componentwise), and the finite generation of J^0(S) is only clear when J^0 is a torus (unit theorem). For a semi-abelian or abelian part one would need Mordell-Weil-Lang-Néron, which is hardly 'élémentaire'.

ideas.what: Profinite Kummer map H^0(S,J) → H^1(S,T_∞ J) obtained from the projective limit of multiplication-by-n isogenies, with kernel the infinitely divisible elements
ideas.modern_name: Kummer map / Kummer theory for commutative group schemes
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Kummer, Weil, Lang); standard in étale cohomology
ideas.where_published: Kummer sequences in SGA 4 / SGA 4½ style étale cohomology; also used implicitly in the anabelian letter to Faltings (1983)

ideas.what: Injectivity of the Kummer map over reduced bases of finite type over Z because the group of sections is finitely generated (units of finitely generated rings)
ideas.modern_name: Kummer injectivity over finitely generated fields/bases (used in anabelian geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: unit theorem: Dirichlet/Samuel/Lang; anabelian use: Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki
ideas.where_published: Spirit of the letter to Faltings and the Esquisse; exact statement unsure

ideas.what: Recovering the distinguished section e (the 'elliptic' datum) from the 2-torsion étale covers plus the T_∞-torsor F_∞(X̃/S)
ideas.modern_name: anabelian reconstruction of sections via Kummer classes
ideas.usually_credited_to: anabelian program (Grothendieck; later Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki)
ideas.where_published: Unpublished Longue Marche continuation; general philosophy in the letter to Faltings

missed.claim: An explicit worked instance of the anabelian principle 'points are determined by their Kummer/torsor classes over finitely generated bases', applied to a tower F_∞(X̃/S) attached to an elliptic-type curve within the Longue Marche manuscript. The technique is now standard; only the specific application is undocumented.
missed.quote: Dans le cas où S est réduit et de type fini sur Z ... on sait (et c'est "élémentaire") que ce noyau est réduit à zéro. Cela signifie donc que la section e ... est donc entièrement déterminée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it shows Grothendieck using Kummer injectivity as a reconstruction tool in the Longue Marche, matching later anabelian methods. Mathematically it is routine.

deep.surprise_reason: Standard Kummer-theory argument (injectivity from finite generation of units). The only interest is the documented use of a Kummer-injectivity reconstruction step in the unpublished Longue Marche continuation.
transcription_corrections: Equation label read as '(324)' is probably '(32''')' or a similar 32-series label continuing (32), (32'), (32'').
'jacobienne[?] elliptique' is uncertain; the image may read 'fonction/courbe elliptique'.
Notation varies between J^0_{U/S} (previous page) and 𝒥°_{u/S}; same object.
